guard_streams.source: Latest telecoms and pay-TV complaints revealed - Q4 2025

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Q4 2025 complaints update on 11 May 2026.
The figures cover October to December 2025.
Overall complaints increased quarter-on-quarter for the first time since 2023.
Broadband and landline complaints decreased during the quarter.
TalkTalk and Vodafone were the most complained-about broadband providers, while Plusnet and Virgin Media were the least complained-about.

guard_streams.source: Quicker complaints resolution and more money in your pocket when things go wrong

facts.detail: Ofcom published the strengthened complaints-resolution update on 8 April 2026.
The waiting period before unresolved complaints can be taken to ADR was reduced from eight weeks to six.
ADR schemes are independent bodies that assess unresolved complaints between customers and providers.
The automatic-compensation scheme covers qualifying broadband and landline service failures.
Automatic compensation payment amounts increased in line with inflation.

guard_streams.source: Money saving tips for phone, broadband and pay-TV

facts.detail: Ofcom published the money-saving guidance on 1 July 2026.
The guidance highlights social tariffs for people receiving qualifying benefits.
Ofcom says service contracts are typically 12, 18 or 24 months long.
Providers must tell customers when contracts are ending and how much they could save on a new deal.
Ofcom notes that some gaining providers may contribute toward exit fees for customers who switch.

guard_streams.source: BDUK delivery performance, quarterly: October 2025 to Dec 2025

facts.detail: BDUK published the quarterly official statistics on 19 February 2026.
The release covers delivery between 1 October and 31 December 2025.
The release also presents revised figures for earlier time periods.
The statistics count premises receiving gigabit-capable coverage as a result of BDUK subsidy.
The release package includes a bulletin, data tables, QMI and a pre-release access list.

guard_streams.source: Quality and methodology information for BDUK delivery performance, quarterly

facts.detail: The QMI explains data strengths, limitations, methods and suitable uses.
BDUK uses geographic lookups from ONS, NISRA, the Scottish Government and AddressBase Premium.
BDUK uses the most recent Ofcom Connected Nations premises and postcode data available.
For the October-to-December 2025 report, 69% of voucher premises used the direct method and 31% used a multiplier method.
The direct expected-premises method applies 5% attrition, while the multiplier method applies 18%.
